entities.name: Greek Dowry System
entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: Greek marriage required the bride's father to provide a substantial dowry (proix) — land, money, or goods. The dowry legally belonged to the wife but was managed by the husband. If divorced, the full dowry had to be returned. A woman without a dowry was essentially unmarriageable.
